title_en: Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Legal Issues Concerning Domestic Waterway Cargo Transportation Dispute Cases
keywords_en: contract dispute; transportation contract; dispute concerning domestic waterway cargo transportation
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Guiding Opinions on Legal Issues in Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport Dispute Cases

Fa Fa [2012] No. 28

The High People's Courts of Liaoning, Tianjin, Shandong, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Hubei, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan (autonomous region/municipality), and the Dalian, Tianjin, Qingdao, Shanghai, Ningbo, Wuhan, Xiamen, Guangzhou, Beihai, and Haikou Maritime Courts:

In recent years, domestic waterway transport has developed rapidly and has played an important role in promoting the development of the national economy. The healthy and orderly development of the waterway transport market depends on a good market environment and complete legal guarantees. However, compared with international maritime transport, which has a relatively complete legal system, the lag in domestic waterway transport laws and regulations has become increasingly prominent, to a certain extent causing an increase in domestic waterway cargo transport dispute cases. China currently has no specific legislation for inland waterway shipping; the regulations and provisions for inland waterway shipping are mostly departmental rules, there are contradictions between the legal and regulatory systems, and there are many inconsistencies in maritime adjudication. In order to strengthen the protective role of China's maritime justice for domestic waterway transport and to promote the standardized development of domestic waterway transport, the following guiding opinions are now put forward on certain legal issues in the trial of domestic waterway cargo transport dispute cases by the people's courts:

I. Respect party autonomy, accurately apply laws and regulations, and unify the adjudication standards for domestic waterway cargo transport dispute cases

The domestic waterway cargo transport disputes referred to in these Guiding Opinions refer to coastal and inland waterway cargo transport disputes that fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of maritime courts.

1. When hearing cases involving disputes over domestic waterway cargo transport contracts, the people's courts shall apply the relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the Contract Law, and other laws, and may also refer to the relevant provisions of the Rules for Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport. The provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code on contracts of carriage of goods by sea are not applicable to domestic waterway cargo transport. When the people's courts refer to the Rules for Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport to determine the rights and obligations of the parties, they shall cite and discuss them in the reasoning section of the judgment, but shall not cite them as the legal basis for the judgment.

2. If the parties clearly stipulate in the domestic waterway cargo waybill or other transport contract documents that their rights and obligations are subject to the provisions of the Rules for Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport, the people's courts may determine the rights and obligations of the parties to the contract in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Rules for Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport.

II. Lawfully determine the validity of domestic waterway cargo transport contracts and maintain the order of the domestic waterway cargo transport market

3. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulations on the Administration of Domestic Waterway Transport and the Provisions on the Administration of Operational Qualifications for Domestic Waterway Transport, enterprises and individuals engaged in domestic waterway transport shall meet and maintain the corresponding operational qualification conditions and engage in waterway transport business activities within the approved scope of operations. For a domestic waterway cargo transport contract entered into by a carrier that has not obtained the operational qualifications for domestic waterway transport, the people's court shall determine the contract to be invalid in accordance with the provisions of Article 52(5) of the Contract Law.

4. If a domestic waterway cargo transport contract is invalid, but the carrier has safely transported the goods to the agreed location in accordance with the terms of the transport contract, and the carrier requests the shipper or consignee to pay the freight by reference to the terms of the contract, the people's court may provide appropriate protection.

If a domestic waterway cargo transport contract is invalid, and the goods are damaged or lost during transport, and the shipper or consignee claims compensation for losses from the carrier, the people's court may comprehensively consider the degree of fault of the shipper or consignee and the carrier regarding the invalidity of the contract and the loss of goods, and determine the corresponding civil liability in accordance with the law.

5. If, during the trial of a domestic waterway cargo transport dispute case, the people's court discovers that the carrier engaged in domestic waterway cargo transport has not obtained the corresponding transport operational qualifications, it shall promptly issue a judicial suggestion to the relevant competent administrative authority.

III. Lawfully hear disputes over domestic waterway cargo transport contracts, accurately determine the liability of the contracting carrier and the actual carrier, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties

6. If the contracting carrier of domestic waterway cargo transport entrusts all or part of the transport to an actual carrier for performance, and the shipper or consignee asserts its rights against the contracting carrier and/or the actual carrier in respect of all or part of the transport, the people's court shall accurately determine the legal status and legal liability of the contracting carrier and the actual carrier. The people's court may determine the liability for compensation of the contracting carrier and the actual carrier by reference to the provisions of Article 46 of the Rules for Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport, fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of the shipper or consignee under the domestic waterway cargo transport contract, and reduce the litigation burden on the parties.

IV. Accurately understand the legal provisions on lien and properly adjudicate lien disputes

7. After the performance of a domestic waterway cargo transport contract is completed, if the shipper or consignee fails to pay the freight, storage fees, or other transport charges as agreed, the carrier shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 315 of the Contract Law, have a lien over the corresponding transported goods. When reviewing the carrier's lien, the people's court shall focus on examining whether the quantity of goods retained by the carrier is within a reasonable limit and whether the goods retained by the carrier are goods lawfully in its possession. Whether the debtor has ownership of the retained goods does not necessarily affect the exercise of the carrier's lien, unless the parties to the transport contract have otherwise specially agreed on the carrier's lien.

V. Properly adjudicate disputes related to ship affiliations, effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, and maintain the orderly development of the domestic waterway transport market

8. The actual owner of an individual transport vessel without operational qualifications, in order to enter the domestic waterway cargo transport market and circumvent the state's regulatory provisions on waterway transport operational qualifications, registers the ownership of the vessel under the name of a ship transport enterprise that has waterway transport operational qualifications, pays management fees to that transport enterprise, and engages in domestic waterway cargo transport activities in the name of that transport enterprise. This is a common practice of affiliated operation in domestic waterway cargo transport. This affiliated operation method renders the ownership registration of the affiliated vessel nominal, causes chaos in vessel management, causes the affiliated enterprise to neglect safety management of the affiliated vessel, seriously impacts the safety order of the shipping market, and leads to the generation of a large number of domestic waterway cargo transport disputes. When hearing contract disputes related to ship affiliations, the people's courts shall strictly determine the legal relationship in accordance with current legal norms on vessel management, adhere to the basic principle of privity of contract, and accurately determine the parties to the contract based on the basic facts such as the parties who signed the contract and the performance of the contract.

9. If the actual owner of an affiliated vessel signs a transport contract in its own name, it shall be determined as the carrier under the transport contract and bear the corresponding contractual liability.

10. If the actual owner of an affiliated vessel signs a transport contract in the name of the affiliated enterprise, and the affiliated enterprise also affixes its seal to confirm, it shall be determined that the affiliated enterprise is the carrier under the transport contract and bears the corresponding contractual liability.

11. In the absence of a signed waterway cargo transport contract, the carrier under the transport contract may be determined based on the record of the carrier on the waybill. If only the vessel name seal of the carrying vessel is affixed to the waybill, it shall be determined that the registered owner of that carrying vessel is the carrier under the transport contract and bears the corresponding contractual liability.

12. If an affiliated vessel causes damage to another person's property or personal injury due to a tort, the actual owner of the affiliated vessel and the affiliated enterprise shall bear joint and several liability for compensation in accordance with the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the Tort Liability Law, the Maritime Code, and relevant judicial interpretations.

VI. Correctly apply the legal provisions on the statute of limitations system and protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties

13. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Question of How to Determine the Limitation Period for Claims for Compensation for Coastal and Inland Waterway Cargo Transport (Fa Shi [2001] No. 18) does not contain special provisions on the suspension or interruption of the statute of limitations for claims for compensation for domestic waterway cargo transport. The people's courts shall apply the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law on the suspension and interruption of the statute of limitations.

December 24, 2012
